title: The fixed--modular integer programming tractability conjecture
statement:
Let $\Delta \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be fixed. An integer program of the form (IP) has a constraint matrix $B$ that is **$\Delta$-modular** if its full-rank minors have absolute value at most $\Delta$ and at least one has absolute value $\Delta$.

**Fixed-$\Delta$ tractability conjecture.** There is a polynomial-time algorithm to solve any integer program of the form (IP) with a $\Delta$-modular constraint matrix.

This conjecture extends the polynomial-time solvability of totally unimodular integer programs to every fixed bound on the maximal non-vanishing subdeterminants. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Björn Kriepke, Gohar M. Kyureghyan and Matthias Schymura, “On the size of integer programs with bounded non-vanishing subdeterminants”, arXiv:2309.03772 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03772

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).
